# Edge Cases Checklist: Branches & Hubs Module

**Purpose**: Validate that the requirements for schedule validation, enum constraints, soft-delete
behavior, and branch-name uniqueness are complete, unambiguous, and internally consistent —
before implementation relies on them.
**Created**: 2026-08-17
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature
context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact.
Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is
satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements
quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Schedule Validation Requirements

- [ ] CHK001 Is the exact behavior specified when a submission contains multiple simultaneous schedule violations (e.g., a duplicate day *and* an invalid time range in the same request) — is every problem reported, or only the first one found? [Ambiguity, Spec §User Story 1 AC3]
- [ ] CHK002 Are the time format, granularity (e.g., minute-level precision), and time zone (branch-local vs. a fixed reference zone) for `opensAt`/`closesAt` specified anywhere in the requirements? [Gap] — _Partially resolved: time zone is resolved (FR-019, branch-local), and format is now documented (`HH:mm:ss`, research.md Decision 13). Granularity/precision (e.g., is a 30-second opening time meaningful?) remains unaddressed — left unchecked for that reason._
- [ ] CHK003 Is behavior defined for a schedule entry whose hours span midnight (e.g., open 22:00–02:00), or is that scenario implicitly out of scope? [Gap, Edge Case]
- [ ] CHK004 Is the requirement rejecting a schedule entry with an unrecognized/invalid day-of-week value stated explicitly, independent of the "no duplicate days" and "exactly 7 entries" rules that only implicitly catch it? [Completeness, Spec §FR-005]
- [x] CHK005 Does the spec reconcile the literal original request language ("must have at least one schedule entry") with the now-confirmed "exactly 7 entries" rule, so a future reader relying on FR-004 alone isn't misled by the earlier phrasing preserved in the Input section? [Consistency, Spec §FR-004] — _Reviewed: FR-004 states "exactly one schedule entry for each of the 7 days ... at all times" without qualification, and the Assumptions section explicitly confirms this was resolved during clarification; the Input section's original phrasing is expected to stay verbatim as a record of the request, not as an active rule._
- [x] CHK006 Is the "opening time strictly earlier than closing time" rule's edge case of exact equality distinguished clearly from times where opening is later than closing, with both explicitly covered? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006] — _Reviewed: "strictly earlier" (FR-006) unambiguously covers both equality and opening-after-closing as rejected; the Edge Cases section spells out the equality case explicitly._

## Enum Constraint Requirements

- [x] CHK007 Is the behavior specified when `CreateBranch`/`UpdateBranch` receives a branch type value outside the four defined types (Headquarters, Hub, SalesPoint, PickupPoint) — the edge cases section only addresses invalid types on the *listing* filter, not on create/update? [Gap, Spec §Edge Cases] — _Resolved during clarification: FR-001 and the Edge Cases section now state this is a validation error on create/update, same treatment as the list filter._
- [ ] CHK008 Does the spec clarify whether the four branch types carry any distinct business rules or data requirements, or explicitly confirm they share identical validation regardless of type? [Ambiguity, Spec §Key Entities]
- [ ] CHK009 Is there a requirement governing how the fixed set of branch types may change over time (e.g., adding a fifth type) and what happens to existing branches of a retired type? [Gap]
- [x] CHK010 Are the acceptable representations of an enum value in a request (e.g., name vs. numeric code, case sensitivity) addressed at the requirements level for both branch type and day-of-week? [Gap] — _Resolved during implementation: both `type` and `dayOfWeek` are accepted/returned as the enum's name (e.g., `"Hub"`, `"Monday"`), never the numeric code, verified against the running API (research.md Decision 12). Documented in contracts/branches-api-contract.md._

## Soft Delete / Deactivation Requirements

- [x] CHK011 Does the spec define what happens to other records that reference a branch (e.g., shipments routed through it) when that branch is deactivated? [Gap] — _Resolved as an explicit scope boundary: the Assumptions section now states this module defines no relationship between Branch and other entities, so deactivation has no defined cross-module effect._
- [x] CHK012 Is it specified whether an inactive branch can still be selected/referenced by operations outside this module, or whether deactivation blocks such usage? [Gap] — _Same Assumption covers this: no such relationship or usage is defined in this module's scope._
- [x] CHK013 Is it explicit whether a branch's non-status fields (address, schedule, coordinates) may be edited via update while the branch is inactive, given the acceptance scenarios for updates (US3) are only written against an "active branch"? [Ambiguity, Spec §User Story 3] — _Resolved during clarification: FR-008 now states updating is never restricted or gated behind reactivation, and US3 gained acceptance scenario 5 covering this exact case._
- [ ] CHK014 Beyond "no error," is the idempotent-deactivation requirement measurable — does it state that repeating the action leaves every other field of the branch unchanged? [Measurability, Spec §FR-011]
- [ ] CHK015 Does the spec define any last-modified/audit tracking requirement for a branch (only `CreatedAt` is defined), given that deactivation and updates are state changes with no defined "when did this last change" signal? [Gap]

## Branch Name Uniqueness Requirements

- [x] CHK016 Does the spec define any uniqueness constraint on branch name scoped to city, as distinct from the documented system-wide "no uniqueness constraint" assumption? [Gap, Spec §Assumptions] — _Resolved during clarification: a per-city rule was explicitly considered and rejected; the "no uniqueness constraint" rule is confirmed to apply system-wide, including within the same city._
- [x] CHK017 Is the "no uniqueness constraint on branch name" assumption's own example (two "Downtown" branches in *different* cities) reconciled with the unaddressed case of two same-named branches in the *same* city? [Consistency, Spec §Assumptions] — _Resolved: the Assumptions bullet now explicitly covers "the same city or in different cities."_
- [x] CHK018 If a per-city name-uniqueness rule were adopted, is the comparison semantics (case sensitivity, whitespace/diacritics normalization, exact vs. fuzzy match) specified anywhere to guide that rule's definition? [Gap] — _Moot: the clarification confirmed no uniqueness rule of any kind is adopted, so no comparison semantics are needed._
- [x] CHK019 Is the conflict/error behavior for a would-be duplicate name-within-city submission defined, in the same way FR-016 defines not-found behavior? [Gap] — _Moot for the same reason as CHK018 — there is no duplicate-name rejection path because no uniqueness constraint exists._
- [x] CHK020 Is "city" alone established as a sufficient uniqueness scope, given that city names are not globally unique across states (e.g., multiple states have a "Springfield") and the entity also carries `state`/`zipCode`? [Ambiguity] — _Moot for the same reason — no city-scoped uniqueness rule exists to scope._
